test_title: SSC CPO 2024 Official Paper-I (Held On: 28 Jun, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions about the right of the Advocate General of a state to speak in the State Legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 177**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 177** of the Indian Constitution mentions the right of the Advocate-General of a state to speak in the State Legislature.
 
• The Advocate-General has the right to be present and speak in both Houses of the State Legislature or any committee thereof, but he does not have the right to vote.
 
• This provision ensures that the Advocate-General can provide legal advice and insights during legislative discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Advocate-General** is the highest law officer in a state, appointed by the Governor of the state.
 
• The Advocate-General's duties include advising the state government on legal matters and representing the state in legal proceedings.
 
• The position of Advocate-General is analogous to that of the Attorney General of India at the national level.
 
• The Advocate-General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor and receives remuneration as determined by the Governor.
